children: A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks pulled back from the previous session's sharp rally, dragging down technology-heavy indexes.

CNBC reported that the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.5% and the S&P 500 edged lower by 1.2%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average traded around the flatline. According to the report, Nvidia shares tumbled more than 7% after soaring 31% in the previous session, while Anthropic tumbled 9%, breaking below its IPO price.

Other artificial intelligence-linked companies also declined, with Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices plunging more than 10%, Broadcom falling 3% and Oracle falling more than 3%, the report said. Mark Haefele, chief investment officer at UBS Global Wealth Management, noted that cloud growth and demand for computing capacity remain supportive, though his team expected greater differentiation between established platforms with strong balance sheets and companies reliant on debt, scarce capacity or speculative growth, according to the report.

When leading artificial intelligence and semiconductor companies pull back sharply, investors often reduce exposure across data center, hardware, and technology infrastructure providers tied to the same spending cycle. Concerns about balance sheet strength and capital intensity can amplify selling in smaller or more leveraged industry peers during a broad tech downturn.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

IREN’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 121 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for IREN and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 1 day ago when the stock gained 30.1% on the news that Nvidia announced the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as president and CEO, sparking renewed investor confidence across artificial intelligence and semiconductor markets following the previous week's sharp downturn. The leadership news lifted broader market indexes as investors stepped back into artificial intelligence and data center operators, reversing a steep retreat that had recently pushed major market benchmarks into correction territory. A market correction occurs when an index declines by 10 percent or more from its recent peak, underscoring the severity of the prior sell-off. Technology and semiconductor shares led the advance during early trading, signaling that investor sentiment has stabilized across the wider chip ecosystem.

IREN is down 69.8% since the beginning of the year, and at $12.88 per share, it is trading 81% below its 52-week high of $67.84 from May 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of IREN’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $641.55.
